source_title: Premium: AI Is Getting Way Too Expensive
other_side: NLW's lead is that capability has outrun our ability to judge it, and that the overhang between what models can already do and what we have built around them is the commercial opportunity. Zitron, three days earlier, argues that this entire register of conversation is the distraction. His case is that debating what LLMs can theoretically do — the jobs, the productivity, the frontier demonstrations — is, in his words, "masturbatory and a conscious attempt to avoid" the messier subject of the money already committed against those promises. He puts trailing industry revenue at roughly $110 billion including OpenAI's and Anthropic's own cloud spend, less than OpenAI raised in a single March round, and argues the arithmetic gets worse as the bubble inflates: infrastructure becomes more expensive to build, so hyperscalers and neoclouds must charge more for compute, and the only two customers big enough to pay cannot afford it. On his reading, a $200 proof is a demonstration, not a business.
truth_beneath: Both men orbit one variable: whether frontier capability converts into revenue faster than the capital committed to producing it comes due. They agree on more than the rhetoric suggests — that today's models can already do things almost nobody has operationalised, and that the applied layer, not the lab, is where any money would have to be made. The empirical question that will resolve is unit economics at the frontier: the observable that settles it is audited inference gross margin at a leading lab, alongside the effective price of a frontier-grade reasoning task twelve months from now. The residue is pure worldview — whether an unverifiable capability is worth paying for at all. NLW is vindicated if applied products built on this overhang generate durable third-party revenue while frontier costs keep falling. Zitron is vindicated if compute prices rise, margins stay negative, and the demonstrations never leave the demo. Both are polemicists with incentives — NLW bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — and the signal is that both now treat raw capability as settled and the money as the open question. Watch what a proof like this costs at list price a year from now.
